title: IMP System Change Notification
publisher_or_issuer: Network Working Group / RFC Editor archival corpus
redistribution_notes: Prefer the RFC Editor canonical copy and metadata unless repository mirroring is independently useful.

provenance.original_holder: ARPANET Network Working Group / BBN publication stream
provenance.chain_notes: Contemporary BBN field-change notification for IMP software version 2514.

claims_extracted.claim: RFC 271 schedules IMPSYS version 2514 for field installation on 13 January 1972 and identifies two version-2513 problems in the delay after a Host comes up before its IMP accepts a second packet.
claims_extracted.locator: RFC 271, page 1, first two substantive paragraphs
claims_extracted.notes: This is a planned installation date, not by itself proof that every site successfully cut over on that date.

claims_extracted.claim: RFC 271 says version 2513 had lengthened the Host-up second-packet delay to slightly over 40 seconds and could ambiguously extend it to about 75 seconds; version 2514 restores the delay to 30 seconds and removes the ambiguity.
claims_extracted.locator: RFC 271, page 1, discussion of the two principal version-2513 problems
claims_extracted.notes: The document also notes that Report 1822 allowed a 30-to-90-second range for this Host-up delay.

claims_extracted.claim: RFC 271 separately states that if a message remains on a Host output queue for 30 seconds the IMP drops its Ready line for one quarter second to clear the interface, cites RFC 270, and explicitly says this queue timeout and the Host-up delay are not synchronized.
claims_extracted.notes: This distinguishes the RFC 270 correction from the separate 2513-to-2514 Host-up timing change.

claims_extracted.claim: RFC 271 requires a Host to be prepared to accept network messages immediately when it indicates that it is alive, even while the IMP is still limiting packets accepted from that Host.
claims_extracted.notes: This is asymmetric interface behavior: receive readiness is immediate while Host-to-IMP acceptance remains temporarily constrained.

notes: The apparent 30-versus-40-second contradiction with RFC 270 disappears once the two independently timed conditions are separated.
